3. Theoretical Frameworks to Enhance Gen Z Engagement and Performance

The increasing diversity and complexity of the modern workforce necessitate the adoption of theoretical frameworks that cater to the unique needs and preferences of Gen Z employees. This section explores two prominent theoretical frameworks that can enhance Gen Z engagement and performance: Self-Determination Theory (SDT) and Transformational Leadership.

1. Self-Determination Theory (SDT): A Multidimensional Approach to Enhancing Gen Z Engagement

Self-Determination Theory (Deci & Ryan, 2000) posits that human behavior is motivated by three innate psychological needs: autonomy, competence, and relatedness. When these needs are satisfied, individuals experience intrinsic motivation, which is essential for sustained engagement and performance. In the context of Gen Z employees, SDT suggests that empowerment through flexible work models and self-directed projects can foster autonomy, leading to increased job satisfaction and reduced turnover intentions (Hackman & Oldham, 1976).

Moreover, opportunities for continual learning and skill development can satisfy the competence need, promoting a sense of mastery and self-efficacy (Bandura, 1997). By providing Gen Z employees with the autonomy to take ownership of their work and develop new skills, organizations can tap into their intrinsic motivation, leading to enhanced performance and productivity.

Finally, fostering a supportive workplace culture that promotes collaboration and social interaction can satisfy the relatedness need, enhancing feelings of belonging and connection among employees (Cohen et al., 2015). By creating a work environment that values diversity, inclusivity, and teamwork, organizations can foster a sense of community and social support, leading to increased job satisfaction and reduced turnover intentions.

2. Transformational Leadership: A Catalyst for Gen Z Engagement and Performance

Transformational Leadership (Bass, 1985) is a leadership style that emphasizes the importance of inspiring and motivating employees to achieve exceptional performance. In the context of Gen Z employees, transformational leadership can be particularly effective in fostering engagement and performance.

Leaders who articulate a compelling vision that resonates with Gen Z's values and interests can inspire and motivate employees to work towards a common goal (Harter et al., 2002). By providing intellectual stimulation and encouraging innovation and critical thinking, leaders can foster a culture of creativity and problem-solving, leading to enhanced performance and productivity (Amabile, 1993).

Moreover, individualized consideration and attention to individual developmental needs and career aspirations can satisfy the competence need, promoting a sense of mastery and self-efficacy (Bandura, 1997). By recognizing and valuing the unique strengths and talents of each employee, leaders can foster a sense of autonomy and self-efficacy, leading to increased job satisfaction and reduced turnover intentions.
